question: Distinguish between a provision and a contingent liability under AS 29 'Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets'.
sources: AS 29 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets - definitions, recognition and disclosure

points.label: Meaning of provision
points.description: A provision is a liability that can be measured only by using a substantial degree of estimation.

points.label: Recognition of a provision
points.description: A provision is recognised when there is a present obligation from a past event, an outflow of resources to settle it is probable, and a reliable estimate can be made.

points.label: Meaning of contingent liability
points.description: A possible obligation whose existence will be confirmed only by uncertain future events not wholly within the enterprise's control, or a present obligation not recognised because an outflow is not probable or the amount cannot be estimated reliably.

points.label: Treatment of contingent liability
points.description: A contingent liability is not recognised in the accounts; it is disclosed unless the possibility of an outflow is remote.
points.basis: AS 29, contingent liabilities: recognition and disclosure

points.label: Review
points.description: Provisions are reviewed at each balance sheet date and adjusted to the current best estimate; contingent liabilities are assessed continually, and if an outflow becomes probable a provision is recognised.
points.basis: AS 29, changes in provisions and assessment of contingent liabilities
